output.brief: The fall is mainly caused by two changes working together, not by the app or the renewal alone. Millbrook kept its coordinator and has stayed on RotaWeave since March, and its active regulars barely moved (118 to 111). Quarry Lane lost its coordinator but never got the app and held roughly steady (86 to 80). Dock Street and Westgate lost both, and their regulars dropped sharply. The mechanism is clear: the app's basic tier has no recurring bookings, so staff used to rebook regulars into their weekly slots before Thursday's release. That booking fell from about 74 a week to 3. Of the April regulars who lost their slot, 88% are now inactive, against 11% who kept it. Background checks are not the driver: 121 of 123 lapsed volunteers had a current check. Confidence is moderate-to-good, but the link rests on one reconciliation and a small callback sample. Next steps: restore a named booking person with an admin seat at Dock Street and Westgate, and phone lapsed regulars to offer their old slots. Keep RotaWeave and the renewal rule, which the county contract and insurer require. Do not remove inactive volunteers from the figures before the board meets. Review in 60 days.
